questiontext.text:
Solve each inequality. Choose the sign and type the number.

(a) {@sa@}

\(x\) [[input:ans1]] [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) {@sb@}

\(x\) [[input:ans3]] [[input:ans4]] [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) Subtract \({@c@}x\) from both sides: \({@lfs([[a-c,"x"],[b,""]])@} {@relt(rela)@} {@d@}\). [[if test="is(b>0)"]]Subtract \({@b@}\)[[else]]Add \({@-b@}\)[[/if]] on both sides: \({@lfs([[a-c,"x"]])@} {@relt(rela)@} {@d-b@}\). Divide both sides by \({@a-c@}\), a positive number, so the sign stays the same: {@ansa@}. Check with \(x = {@cha@}\): the left side is \({@a*cha+b@}\) and the right side is \({@c*cha+d@}\), and the statement is true.

(b) Method 1: subtract \({@p@}\) from both sides: \({@lfs([[-q,"x"]])@} {@relt(relb)@} {@r-p@}\). Divide both sides by \({@-q@}\). Dividing by a negative number turns the sign round: {@ansb@}.

Method 2: add \({@lfs([[q,"x"]])@}\) to both sides so that no negative number is involved: \({@p@} {@relt(relb)@} {@lfs([[r,""],[q,"x"]])@}\). Subtract \({@r@}\) from both sides: \({@p-r@} {@relt(relb)@} {@lfs([[q,"x"]])@}\), so \({@nd(kb)@} {@relt(relb)@} x\), which is the same as {@ansb@}.

Check with \(x = {@chb@}\): the left side is \({@p-q*chb@}\), and \({@p-q*chb@} {@relt(relb)@} {@r@}\) is true.

questiondescription.text:
Linear Inequalities: solving simple inequalities

Grade 12 CBE Essential 1.3: Solve a linear inequality with the unknown on both sides, and one with a negative coefficient of the unknown.

Essential

This question is adapted from Chapter 28 (Solving inequalities), Sections D and E, questions D3 and E4 of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 1 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2006: new inequalities, with the sign and the boundary entered separately.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

falsefeedback.text: The value is right, but you turned the sign round. You divided by \({@a-c@}\), which is positive, so the sign stays the same way round.

node.description: Moved b with the wrong sign

truefeedback.text: Check the step where you move \({@b@}\): to remove it from the left side, [[if test="is(b>0)"]]subtract \({@b@}\)[[else]]add \({@-b@}\)[[/if]] on both sides, so the right side becomes \({@d-b@}\).
To collect the \(x\) terms, subtract \({@c@}x\) from both sides. That leaves \({@a-c@}x\) on the left, not \({@a+c@}x\).

falsefeedback.text: At the boundary value the two sides are equal. With \(x = {@nd(xr)@}\) the left side is \({@nd(a*xr+b)@}\) and the right side is \({@nd(c*xr+d)@}\). Collect the \(x\) terms on the left and the numbers on the right, then divide by the number in front of \(x\).

truefeedback.text: The value {@ndm(kb)@} is right, but check the sign: [[if test="strictp(trb)"]]the question's sign is strict, so yours must be too[[else]]the question's sign includes equal to, so yours must too[[/if]].

falsefeedback.text: The value is right, but the sign must turn round. When you divide both sides by \({@-q@}\), the order is reversed: \(2 \lt 3\) but \(-2 \gt -3\). Or add \({@q@}x\) to both sides first so that no negative number is involved.

truefeedback.text: You divided by \({@q@}\) instead of \({@-q@}\). The term is \({@lfs([[-q,"x"]])@}\).

node.description: Moved p with the wrong sign

truefeedback.text: Subtract \({@p@}\) from both sides first: the right side becomes \({@r-p@}\).

falsefeedback.text: At the boundary value the two sides are equal. With \(x = {@nd(xr)@}\) the left side is \({@nd(p-q*xr)@}\), not \({@r@}\). Get the \(x\) term on its own, then divide by its coefficient. Dividing by a negative number turns the sign round.
